st: Boil the split peas in the water with the turmeric for 25 minutes until just tender but not mushy.
Drain well and cool for 10 minutes. Grind in a food processor to a crumbly, dry meal with the cumin, garlic, chili powder and [[1 tsp]] of the salt.
Mix the flour, remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] of the oil. Add warm water to make a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Flatten one ball, put about [[2 tbsp]] of the pea mixture in the middle, and pinch the dough closed around it.
Flatten gently with a rolling pin into a thin circle about 7 inches wide, without letting the filling break through.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook each puri for 1 to 2 minutes per side, brushing with a little of the remaining oil, until pale gold with light spots.
Keep the puris wrapped in a clean towel. Serve warm with curry or beans.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and brown the sausage slices for 6 minutes. Remove them.
Cook the onion in the pan for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute.
Add the thyme and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and jammy.
Return the sausage to the pan and simmer on low for 10 minutes. The sausage must be fully cooked, with no pink inside.
Taste and adjust the salt. Stir in the scallions.
Serve with rice, lentils or flatbread.
Boil the noodles according to the package until just tender, then drain and rinse with cold water. Toss with [[1 tsp]] of the oil.
Toss the chicken with [[1 tbsp]] of the soy sauce and the pepper.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs for 1 minute and remove.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the chicken for 4 minutes until cooked through.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the carrots for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, remaining soy sauce and eggs and toss for 3 minutes until hot.
Stir in the scallions and sesame oil and serve right away.
Drain the soaked split peas and rinse them.
Grind them in a food processor with a splash of water, until coarse and thick, not smooth.
Mix in the onion, chilies, cilantro, scallions, cumin, garlic and salt.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes. It should hold its shape when scooped.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
With wet hands, shape the batter into balls about 1 inch wide, or drop by spoonfuls into the oil.
Fry in batches for 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels. Cut one open to check that the middle is cooked. Serve hot with chutney.
Pat the fish dry and rub with [[1 tsp]] of the salt and half the turmeric. Dust lightly with flour.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and fry the fish for 3 minutes per side until cooked through. Drain and set aside.
Grind the mustard seeds with half of the vinegar and the water to a rough paste.
In a clean pan, heat the remaining oil and cook the onions for 4 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and chilies for 2 minutes.
Stir in the remaining turmeric and the mustard paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining vinegar and salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour the warm sauce over the fish. Cool, cover, and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or longer, so it can pickle.
Serve at room temperature with rice or bread.
Mix the cornstarch with the water and [[1 tbsp]] of the soy sauce to make a sauce slurry.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 4 minutes until cooked through, then add the shrimp for 2 minutes until pink. Remove both.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil, add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the bok choy for 3 minutes.
Return the meats, add the remaining soy sauce, and pour in the slurry. Cook for 2 minutes until glossy.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the remaining oil with the salt, 2 minutes each.
Grease four bowls lightly. Lay a fried egg in the bottom of each, then top with some stir-fry.
Pack the rice firmly on top.
Turn each bowl upside down onto a plate and lift off the bowl. Sprinkle with scallions and serve.
Mix the flour, sugar and salt. Add [[2 tbsp]] of the oil and the water gradually to form a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide into 6 balls, coat with a little oil, cover, and rest for 40 minutes.
On an oiled counter, stretch or roll one ball into a very thin rectangle.
Brush with melted butter, then roll it up like a rope and coil it into a spiral. Tuck the end in.
Rest the coils for 20 minutes, then flatten each into a thin circle about 7 inches wide.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Cook each farata for 2 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden with flaky layers.
Clap the cooked farata between your hands to open up the layers. Keep wrapped in a towel and serve warm.
Mix the chicken with [[1 tbsp]] of the curry powder, half the garlic and half the salt. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onions for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the remaining garlic, ginger, thyme and remaining curry powder with a splash of water, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the water and remaining salt. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer, covered, 20 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with rice and flatbread.
Soak the basil seeds in [[0.5 cup]] of water for 15 minutes until they swell and turn gel-like.
For the jelly, whisk the agar with [[1 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] of the sugar in a small pot. Boil for 2 minutes.
Pour the jelly into a dish, tint pink with the rose syrup if you like, and chill 20 minutes until firm. Cut into small cubes.
Whisk the milk with the remaining sugar and the vanilla until dissolved. Chill if time allows.
Put a spoonful of soaked basil seeds and some jelly into each tall glass.
Pour in the cold milk and stir well.
Top with a scoop of ice cream if you like. Serve with a long spoon and a straw.
Boil the sweet potatoes for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain and mash until smooth.
Mix the mashed potato with the flour and salt to a soft dough. Add a bit more flour if sticky. Rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the coconut with [[0.25 cup]] of the sugar, the cardamom and water over low heat for 5 minutes until moist and sticky. Cool.
On a floured surface, roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut into circles about 3 inches wide.
Put about [[1 tbsp]] filling on each circle, fold over to make a half moon, and press the edge with a fork.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, then roll in the remaining sugar while warm.
